p1: Long ago, Isaiah wrote about Someone Heavenly Father would send. That Someone would “bind up the brokenhearted.” He would gently wrap very sad hearts, like a bandage on a knee.
He would also give “beauty for ashes.” Long ago, very sad people put gray ashes from a fire on their heads. So ashes meant sadness. He would give beauty and joy instead.
Many years later, Jesus went to the meeting house in His hometown, Nazareth. He stood up and read Isaiah’s words out loud.
p2: Then Jesus sat down, and every eye was on Him. He said, “Today these words have come true.” Isaiah was talking about Jesus!
When your heart feels sad, Jesus can help it heal. He is gentle, and He loves you.
old: Isaiah was a prophet. That means Heavenly Father told him what to say. Heavenly Father's people lived far away from home and they were very sad, so Heavenly Father sent Isaiah to tell them good news.

Isaiah said, "Someone is coming to help you! He will make sad hearts feel better. Some of our people are locked up and cannot go home, and He will open the door and let them out. He will hold everyone who is crying."

Isaiah said Jesus would make a trade. Long ago, when people were very sad, they put grey ashes on their heads so everyone could see how sad they felt. So ashes mean sadness. You can give Jesus your ashes, all the grey, sad, heavy things, and He gives you something beautiful, like flowers in your hair.

Isaiah said one more thing. Long ago, when people were happy, they rubbed sweet-smelling oil on their faces for a party. So Jesus takes away your tears and gives you party oil and a happy song instead. Then your heart grows strong and tall, like a little tree that Heavenly Father planted Himself. When your heart feels heavy tonight, you can give it to Jesus. He always has something beautiful for you.
